explain.say: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother. Caliban says that in Shakespeare's The Tempest, written around 1611, as English ships were crossing the Atlantic. Postcolonial criticism reads stories from the side of the colonised. The board shows the same play seen two ways.

explain.say: Here are the key thinkers. Look at 1978: Edward Said's Orientalism showed how Western writers invented an East that was exotic, lazy and in need of rule, an image that helped empire. Can you think of a film that still paints a place this way?

explain.say: Sort the key words. In the middle, the subaltern: Gayatri Spivak asked whether people shut out of power can be heard at all, if others always speak for them. On the right, Homi Bhabha's hybridity and mimicry, cultures mixing, copies that unsettle the master. Which word is new to you?

Writers answered back. In 1975 Chinua Achebe gave a lecture attacking Conrad's Heart of Darkness for turning Africans into scenery. His own novel Things Fall Apart, in 1958, told the story from inside an Igbo village. In what language would you write, if you had to choose?

explain.say: Back to the island. Caliban was taught language and lost his land. In 1969 Aime Cesaire rewrote the play with Caliban as a rebel. Wonderful work. Challenge: retell a classic from the point of view of its quietest character.

faq.a: Edward Said's 1978 term for the way Western scholarship, art and literature built an image of the East as exotic, backward and irrational, which supported colonial power.
People shut out of the structures of power, such as colonised peasants or women. Spivak asked in 1988 whether they can be heard when others always speak for them.
When writers from colonised places answer canonical texts, retelling them from the other side, as Achebe answered Conrad or Rhys answered Charlotte Bronte.
asks: What is the empire writes back?

faq.a: Homi Bhabha's terms. Hybridity is the mixing of cultures under colonialism; mimicry is the colonised copying the coloniser, almost the same but not quite, which quietly mocks colonial authority.

faq.q: Why is Caliban important to postcolonial critics?
faq.a: He is a native of the island enslaved by Prospero, who says the island is his. Writers from the Caribbean and Africa have read him as a figure of the colonised.

facts: Edward Said's Orientalism was published in 1978.
Chinua Achebe gave his lecture An Image of Africa in 1975 at the University of Massachusetts.
Aime Cesaire's Une Tempete, a rewriting of The Tempest, appeared in 1969.

quiz.why: Edward Said, a Palestinian-American critic, wrote Orientalism.
